title: SLO-aware Batchline Debug Scratchbook
content:
Overview:
This is a working scratchbook for the "batchline" experiments — an SLO-aware variant of the continuous batching scheduler. The idea: give each request a small "tailbudget" allocation (ms) derived from its SLO, age, and priority. The batchline then forms batches while respecting a global tailbudget budget and per-tenant slot-credit limits. Purpose is to reduce p99/p999 spikes for mixed-length workloads without severely harming throughput.

Why this is different (quick):
- Moves beyond fixed timeouts by accounting for per-request tail budget
- Uses soft credits (slot-credit) to avoid starving low-priority tenants during microbursts
- Tries to shape flush decisions with a tiny ML-calibrated estimator for remaining model time (rough estimate) rather than constant thresholds

Goals / success metrics:
- Primary: reduce p99 by >= 20% on mixed chat+summarization workload under 60% GPU utilization
- Secondary: keep throughput drop <= 10% and median latency degradation <= 5%
- Tertiary: reduce frequency of 5x p99 spikes (events where p99 exceeds 5x baseline p99)

Hypotheses:
H1: Tailbudget-aware flush will convert a portion of p99 spikes into p95 improvements because we avoid flushing big batches early for tiny requests.
H2: Slot-credit backpressure will keep tail starvation low compared to fixed-priority demotion.
H3: Estimator noise matters — if the remaining-token estimator has >30% error, batchline decisions degrade and we see throughput loss.

Workload and test harness:
- Workload: synthetic mix reflecting production inter-arrival and length distribution (60% short chat ~ 20–80 tokens, 30% medium completion ~ 200 tokens, 10% long summaries ~ 1000 tokens). Burstiness profile taken from production replay (sample window: 2025-08-07 12:00–14:00).
- Harness: local cluster of 4x A100-equivalent nodes (dev infra), using trace-replay harness (replay tool v0.9.2).
- Measurement windows: 30m warmup, 1h experiment, 30m cooldown. Aggregations by 5m windows.

Configs tried (labelled):
- BL-BASELINE: current continuous-batcher (fixed timeout 8ms, max-batch 64)
- BL-TB: batchline with tailbudget per request, same max-batch and default slot-credit 4
- BL-TB-EST: BL-TB + estimator enabled (lightweight token-time predictor)
- BL-TB-SC8: BL-TB with slot-credit=8 (more aggressive accumulation)
- BL-TB-FLUSHHYST: BL-TB + hysteresis on flush (minimum hold 2ms after first non-full batch formed)

Quick run notes (commands used):
- ./harness replay --trace ./traces/aug7_mixed.json --config conf/bl-tb.yaml --duration 1h --out results/bl-tb
- profiling: cpuprofiler + nvprof runs attached via staging probe container; profiler flags: --samples-per-sec 500

Results (summary numbers aggregated across 1h window, relative to BL-BASELINE):
- BL-BASELINE: p50 12ms, p95 180ms, p99 420ms, throughput 100k tokens/s (baseline)
- BL-TB: p50 13ms (+8%), p95 140ms (-22%), p99 330ms (-21%), throughput 96k tokens/s (-4%)
- BL-TB-EST: p50 14ms (+16%), p95 130ms (-28%), p99 290ms (-31%), throughput 92k tokens/s (-8%)
- BL-TB-SC8: p50 12.5ms (+4%), p95 150ms (-17%), p99 310ms (-26%), throughput 94k tokens/s (-6%)
- BL-TB-FLUSHHYST: p50 13ms (+8%), p95 135ms (-25%), p99 305ms (-27%), throughput 95k tokens/s (-5%)

Interpretation / notes:
- Tailbudget gating yielded consistent p95/p99 wins across configs while only modestly impacting median/throughput.
- Estimator (BL-TB-EST) gave best tail numbers but increased median/throughput hit; plausible that estimator made more conservative flushes (overestimation of remaining time).
- Slot-credit tuning matters: raising credits to 8 reduces p50 impact but slightly worsens p95 vs estimator configuration. There's a sweet spot around 4–6 for our workload.

Profiling & bottleneck notes:
- Kernel hotspots: attention kernel still dominates per-token GPU time; batch coalescing slightly increases per-kernel occupancy but overall GPU utilization climbed ~8% which explains some throughput drop.
- CPU-side: scheduler lock contention visible during microbursts (stack traces show contention in batch_allocator::allocate_slot). Under BL-TB a new atomic slot-credit operation increased contention at spikes — need to micro-optimize (see below).
- NVTX traces: flush events align with short-request floods; BL-TB shifted flush timing reducing wasted model computation due to early flush of long requests.

Failure / anomaly cases spotted:
- Edgecase: long-running summary requests occasionally exhausted tailbudget and got preempted mid-batch leading to rare 2x p999 spikes (investigate preemption path).
- Under synthetic pathological input (all long, then all short) BL-TB-EST caused oscillation in batch sizes — estimator being reactive to sudden length-phase change. Simple smoothing of estimator predictions fixed oscillation in a follow-up run.

Actionable follow-ups (short):
1) Fix atomic hotpath: replace atomic slot-credit decrement with per-thread batch-local accrual + periodic reconcile (reduce contention). Owner: Diego. ETA: 1 sprint.
2) Add lightweight exponential smoothing to estimator (alpha=0.2) and re-run BL-TB-EST to measure throughput recovery. Owner: Mei. ETA: 1 week.
3) Add a guard in preemption path to avoid midway preemptions of long requests when their remaining tailbudget < 2ms; instead mark for immediate fallback to lower-cost variant. Owner: Omar. ETA: 2 weeks.
4) Run larger cluster/region replay (staging) to validate scalability (8–16 nodes). Owner: Aisha. ETA: next month.

Longer-term / research ideas:
- Integrate small learned cost model per-model-version that predicts expected tail contribution conditioned on prefix tokens and model temperature. Could push estimator error below 20%.
- Global tailbudget marketplace across tenants: trade SLO budget for optional cost bump (premium path).
- Combine with KV cache awareness: if a request is heavily cached, we can be more aggressive grouping it even if long.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Push PR skeleton for slot-credit micro-optim to git (PR link above).
- Add unit tests for preemption guard and estimator smoothing.
- Collect additional traces for 'pathological-phase-change' workload.

Open questions / discussion prompts for next sync:
- Is 10% throughput hit acceptable for 25–30% p99 reduction? Product might accept if p50 degraded <10% and no SLA regressions for paid customers.
- Can we pursue a hybrid mode that toggles estimator on only for high tail-risk tenants?

Appendix: sample config snippet (conf/bl-tb.yaml):

# (note: YAML here as a literal string example)
scheduler:
  mode: batchline
  tailbudget_ms_default: 50
  slot_credit_default: 4
  flush_hysteresis_ms: 2
  estimator:
    enabled: true
    smoothing_alpha: 0.2

Experiment raw logs: results/ (attached in drive folder).

End of scratchbook.
